domain: Strategic asset allocation, house-view implementation and portfolio construction for the ₹500 Cr NDPMS mandate
executive_summary: The non-discretionary constraint, not the asset mix, is the design driver. We propose a pre-agreed Model Master with rebalance bands written into the IPS so the monthly consent pack becomes a short list of band-restoring and TAA trades executed on the existing Thursday cycle. Instruments are chosen for low cost, low turnover and low consent friction: index funds and ETFs via AP creation units for core beta (32–37%), factor index funds (Quality/Low Vol/Momentum) for the house tilt, a 20–25 name direct-stock book from the NIFTY-750 scorecard capped at 8–12%, active MFs only where alpha persistence is documented (mid/small), and high-turnover ideas pushed inside wrappers where the manager holds discretion (Cat III AIF, SIF hybrid long-short, one third-party PMS). NDPMS uniquely permits up to 25% of client AUM in unlisted securities; we use 9% (Moderate) / 12% (Aggressive) for Cat II private credit, long-short and pre-IPO, leaving headroom. Two fully sized books: Moderate — E[R] 10.0%, vol 9.7%, Sharpe 0.42, beta 0.55, GFC-type shock −30%; Aggressive — E[R] 10.9%, vol 12.5%, Sharpe 0.39, beta 0.72, shock −40%; versus the Allocate 80/20 at 10.0% / 13.6% / 0.30 / −43%. We recommend investable composite benchmarks matched to sleeve weights (Moderate: 55% Nifty 500 TRI, 5% S&P 500 INR, 25% CRISIL Composite Bond, 5% gold, 10% Nifty 50 Arbitrage) with the 80/20 house benchmark as a secondary line. Deploy over 8–12 weekly tranches from an arbitrage fund (equity-taxed) with pre-consented acceleration on every −5% Nifty move; expected one-off cash drag ₹2.0–2.5 Cr. Owned controllable cost budget ~125–145 bps p.a., of which realised tax (60–80 bps) is the largest — turnover discipline (TAA ≤10% NAV/month, direct-stock churn <30% p.a.) is therefore a return decision, not an ops nicety. Open legal item: whether a pre-authorised band-execution matrix satisfies the "on client instruction" test; the design works without it.

can_do.item: Pre-agreed Model Master with SAA weights and rebalance bands embedded in the IPS schedule
can_do.what: Sign sleeve weights, per-line bands (core ±5%, satellite ±3%, alternatives ±2%, FI ±3%, gold ±1.5%), composite benchmark and deployment schedule at onboarding as an annexure to the Reg 22 written agreement.
can_do.why: Converts every month's rebalance from a debate into a confirmation; halves consent latency and gives the team a contract to be measured against.
can_do.notes: Reg 22(1) requires written agreement [3]; annexure is the natural home.

can_do.item: Monthly batched consent pack aligned to the Thursday deployment cycle
can_do.what: One document per month: band breaches, TAA tilts with conviction scores, corporate-action elections, cash sweep; client e-signs by Wednesday, execution Thursday.
can_do.why: NDPMS requires instruction per trade; batching is the only way to keep turnover cost and latency bounded.

can_do.item: Standing instruction for band-restoring trades within pre-agreed ranges
can_do.what: Client pre-authorises execution of any trade that only restores a breached band, without fresh sign-off.
can_do.why: Would remove most latency cost; but whether it satisfies the non-discretionary test is not settled.
can_do.notes: Obtain written legal opinion before relying on it; design pack to work without it.

can_do.item: Core beta via Nifty 50/100 ETFs through AP creation units plus index funds (direct plan)
can_do.what: ₹110–125 Cr in 2 ETFs + 1 index fund; orders >₹5 Cr routed to APs (Nifty BeES CU 50,000 units) rather than on-screen.
can_do.why: 3–10 bps TER, unlimited capacity, no price risk during consent lag when using NAV-based index fund orders; equity ETF on-screen ADV only ~₹745 Cr/day [45].

can_do.item: Factor sleeve via index funds (Quality 30, Low Vol 30, Momentum 30)
can_do.what: 10–12% split roughly 5/3/2 (Moderate) or 5/3/4 (Aggressive); TAA tilts expressed here first.
can_do.why: Cheapest way to implement 'overweight large-cap quality'; Quality has lagged 3 years and is cheap [52].
can_do.notes: Momentum capped at 2–4%: crash-prone at turns, 1-yr return ~0% [51].

can_do.item: Direct-stock book of 20–25 quality-tilted names from the NIFTY-750 scorecard, capped at 8–12%
can_do.what: Avg position ₹1.6–2.4 Cr; inclusion needs ADV ≥₹20 Cr; ≤1% of float, ≤20% ADV/day, ≤3% of NAV per name; turnover <30% p.a.
can_do.why: This is where the team's scorecard alpha is owned; but every trade is a consent line, so size and turnover must stay low.

can_do.item: Active mutual funds only for mid/small cap, direct plans, ticket ≤1% of scheme AUM
can_do.what: 2 mid-cap + 1–2 small-cap schemes with ≥₹2,500 Cr AUM; selection bar: 3-yr rolling alpha >150 bps net in ≥60% of windows.
can_do.why: Alpha persistence evidence exists in Indian mid/small, not large cap; Master Circular requires direct plans for PM-routed MF investments [4].

can_do.item: One concentrated third-party PMS (mid/small specialist), ₹10–15 Cr
can_do.what: Client signs the PMS agreement; we monitor holdings overlap with our direct book and style drift.
can_do.why: Access to boutique capacity our MF filter excludes; ₹50 lakh minimum is trivial at this size [1][2].
can_do.notes: Avoid 3+ PMS managers — reporting sprawl and look-through complexity.

can_do.item: Use the NDPMS-only 25% unlisted allowance for Cat II private credit, Cat III long-short and pre-IPO
can_do.what: 9% (Moderate) / 12% (Aggressive) across 6–8 AIF commitments of ₹5–15 Cr each; hard internal cap 15%.
can_do.why: Discretionary PMS cannot hold unlisted; this is the mandate's structural edge and delivers 11–15% pre-tax carry uncorrelated to Nifty [1][2][57].
can_do.notes: AIF units count as unlisted; ₹1 Cr minimum per fund [7]; Cat I/II close-ended ≥3 yrs [60].

can_do.item: SIF hybrid long-short as the preferred long-short wrapper once 12–18 months live track exists
can_do.what: ₹10–20 Cr in 1–2 SIF strategies (₹10 lakh minimum); up to 25% unhedged short allowed inside the wrapper [9][11].
can_do.why: MF-platform taxation likely cheaper than Cat III trust-level tax (~42.7%) [15]; discretion sits with the AMC so no consent per trade.
can_do.notes: Category AUM only ₹13,814 Cr (May 2026) [10]; verify each scheme's tax classification.

can_do.item: Fixed income via target-maturity funds and direct 10-yr G-sec rather than direct corporate paper
can_do.what: Moderate: 11% TMF (AAA PSU/SDL 3–5 yr), 6% 10-yr G-sec/dynamic, 4% AA via credit funds, 3% short duration.
can_do.why: Carry deficit to equity is the lowest in a decade (10-yr at 6.96% vs 11% equity E[R]) [21]; corporate lots are illiquid below a ₹50 Cr sleeve.

can_do.item: Gold 4–5% via ETF (AP route), silver capped at 1%
can_do.what: 1 gold ETF, 1 silver ETF; bands ±1.5% / ±0.5%.
can_do.why: Gold's −0.1 correlation and +25% in 2008-type shocks is the only cheap tail hedge; silver has equity-like vol (26.6%) and −54% max DD [35].

can_do.item: Listed REIT/InvIT sleeve of 4–5 names at 2–4%
can_do.what: Embassy, Mindspace, Brookfield, Nexus, IndiGrid; each ≤₹6 Cr; band ±1%.
can_do.why: 6–10% distribution yield with partial tax-free return of capital; 0.35 correlation [37][38].

can_do.item: International DM equity 5–7% via 2 feeder index funds plus 1 backup route
can_do.what: S&P 500 / MSCI World index funds or FoF; hold in arbitrage if subscription windows close.
can_do.why: 0.45 correlation and INR depreciation tailwind (~3.7% p.a. approx.); but the USD 7 bn industry cap has already paused several AMCs [28][29].
can_do.notes: Overseas direct securities not permitted for PMS today; SEBI Jul-2026 consultation may change this [5][6].

can_do.item: Arbitrage fund (not liquid fund) as the parking and liquidity asset
can_do.what: 2% steady state, 1–4% band; all undeployed equity money during deployment.
can_do.why: 6.7% 1-yr return with equity taxation (12.5% LTCG) vs slab-taxed liquid at 6.4% [48][50]; ~15 bps post-tax advantage for a 39% slab client.

can_do.item: Composite benchmark matched to SAA, with Allocate 80/20 as secondary line
can_do.what: Moderate: 55% Nifty 500 TRI + 5% S&P 500 INR + 25% CRISIL Composite Bond + 5% gold + 10% Nifty 50 Arbitrage; Aggressive: 75/7/8/5/5.
can_do.why: Owning returns requires a benchmark the book can actually hold; TE vs composite 1.5–2.1% vs 3.2–4.8% against 80/20.

can_do.item: TAA sizing by conviction score × tracking-error budget with an evidence bar
can_do.what: tilt = C(−3..+3) × unit (~1.0 pp Moderate, 1.5 pp Aggressive); TE budget 2%/3%; move only if 2 of 3 evidence tests pass (valuation |z|≥1, revision breadth 2 months, scorecard quintile); auto-halve after 6 months.
can_do.why: Turns the IC view into bounded, auditable trades; prevents turnover creep that the tax drag punishes.

can_do.item: Staggered deployment: 8–12 weekly Thursday tranches with pre-consented acceleration rules
can_do.what: Equity-like 8.33%/week (12-wk) or 12.5% (8-wk); FI in 4 weeks; +1 tranche per −5% Nifty from T, +2 at −10%, all-in at −15%; India VIX >22 counts as −5%; never decelerate on rallies.
can_do.why: Expected cash drag ₹2.0–2.5 Cr (12-wk) or ₹1.4–1.7 Cr (8-wk); acceleration rules are pre-consented so no fresh instruction is needed in a sell-off.

can_do.item: Minimum trade size ₹1 Cr and monthly TAA turnover cap 10% of NAV
can_do.what: Drifts smaller than 20 bps wait for next month; aggregate active weight ≤10 pp Moderate / 15 pp Aggressive.
can_do.why: Consent latency cost (~6 bps expected, ±30 bps 1σ) and realised tax (60–80 bps) scale with turnover.

can_do.item: Unlisted-cap and concentration monitor in the daily risk dashboard
can_do.what: Daily check: unlisted ≤25% (alert at 18%), single stock ≤3%, single AIF ≤4%, single MF scheme ticket ≤1% of scheme AUM, gold+silver ≤7%.
can_do.why: Regulatory breach of the 25% cap is a compliance event; AIF NAV lag can push the ratio up in equity drawdowns.

can_do.item: Annual CMA refresh and band/line-count review
can_do.what: Re-estimate E[R], vol, correlations; confirm ≤60 line items and each ≥₹1.5 Cr (silver excepted).
can_do.why: CMAs drift with valuations (Nifty at 20× vs 23× median today); line sprawl kills consent-pack readability.

can_do.item: Intraday, HFT, options overwriting or covered-call programs inside the client account
can_do.what: Any strategy needing same-day execution decisions.
can_do.why: Consent latency makes them uneconomic and arguably non-compliant; if wanted, buy them inside a Cat III AIF or SIF.

can_do.item: Momentum factor >5% standalone in the Moderate book
can_do.what: Large Momentum 30 allocation as a core holding.
can_do.why: Semi-annual reconstitution turnover, −60% approx. drawdowns at regime turns, and 1-yr return near zero [51].

can_do.item: Direct corporate bonds below a ₹50 Cr sleeve, or more than 3 PMS managers, or silver >1%
can_do.what: Concentration and operational sprawl choices that look attractive on yield or diversification grounds.
can_do.why: Illiquid lots, per-ISIN consent lines, reporting complexity, and silver's −54% max DD.

can_do.item: Pooled/omnibus execution across clients or netting against Allocate books
can_do.what: Aggregating orders in a house account.
can_do.why: PMS requires client-name holding and per-client instruction; not permitted.

detailed_markdown:
# Strategic Asset Allocation, House-View Implementation and Portfolio Construction — ₹500 Cr NDPMS Mandate

*Ionic Wealth (Angel One) · Design note for the CIO/PM team · As of 12 Sep 2026. Verified facts carry a bracketed source number; anything marked "approx." is an estimate or an unverified figure. Full file: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-claude-demo/f31f9728-4a4d-5703-8958-ff115211d242/scratchpad/ndpms/design_allocation.md*

## 0. Design stance in one paragraph

The mandate is ₹500 Cr under **non-discretionary** PMS: we recommend, the client consents, we execute. That single constraint drives everything below. We therefore (a) build the portfolio from a **pre-agreed Model Master with rebalance bands** so that the monthly consent pack is a short list of band-restoring and tilt trades rather than a fresh debate; (b) favour instruments that are **cheap to hold, cheap to trade and slow-moving** (index funds, ETFs via APs, target-maturity debt, quality-tilted direct stocks, listed REITs/InvITs) and keep high-turnover ideas inside vehicles where the manager holds the discretion (Cat III AIF, SIF long-short, third-party PMS); (c) use the NDPMS-only privilege of **up to 25% of client AUM in unlisted securities** (AIF units, unlisted debt) [1][2] deliberately but not fully — 9% Moderate / 12% Aggressive — to leave headroom; and (d) own the outcome with a **composite benchmark that is investable and matches the sleeve weights**, with the Allocate 80/20 house benchmark retained as a secondary reference.

Market context that matters for CMAs and deployment today: Nifty 50 ~23,200–23,500, a three-month low, trailing P/E ~19.8–20.2 vs a 10-yr median ~23.3 [23][24][25][26]; FY27E Nifty EPS growth consensus 15–17% but skewed to the downside on crude [27]; 10-yr G-sec 6.96% with repo at 5.25% [21][22]; USD/INR ~95.7 [42]; 10-yr AAA spread over G-sec ~221 bps and 3-yr ~111 bps per one tracker [30][31] (dealers quote AAA PSU 10–60 bps, AAA NBFC 50–140 bps, AA 100–260 bps [32]) — so the term-premium-plus-credit stack is unusually generous relative to the last five years.

---

## 1. Capital-market assumptions (10-year forward, INR, pre-tax, gross of our fees)

Method: forward equity return = dividend yield (~1.2%) + real earnings growth + inflation (~4.5%) ± valuation drift; Nifty 50 at ~20× trailing vs 23× median implies roughly +1% p.a. of valuation tailwind over 10 years, which we net against a slower nominal GDP path than the last decade. Bonds = current YTM ± roll. Gold = INR depreciation (~3.5% approx.) + real-rate/central-bank demand premium. Alternatives = manager target IRR net of fees, haircut 200–300 bps for selection risk. Correlations are to Nifty 50 TRI and are approx. unless sourced.

**Reading the table.** Large cap is priced to deliver ~11% nominal; the "extra" for mid/small is +150–200 bps for +4–8 points of vol and much deeper drawdowns — worth owning through the cycle but sized, not chased. Bonds at 6.6–7.1% with near-zero equity correlation give a 4–5-point carry deficit to equity, the lowest in a decade, so the Moderate book can hold 24% fixed income without a large return sacrifice. Gold's expected 8% is below its trailing 11–15% because the last three years front-loaded the central-bank bid.

---

## 2. Sleeve architecture and instrument-choice logic

### 2.1 Five sleeves

| Sleeve | Purpose | Moderate | Aggressive | Instruments | Rebalance band |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Core beta** | Cheap, capacity-unlimited Indian large cap + factor tilts | 32% | 37% | Nifty 50/100 ETFs (AP creation), index funds; factor index funds | ±5% sleeve / ±2% per factor |
| **Satellite alpha** | Stock/manager selection we own: scorecard direct stocks, active mid/small MFs, 1 PMS, international | 33% | 44% | Direct stocks 20–25 names; 2–3 active MFs; 1 PMS (₹10–15 Cr); 1–2 international index funds | ±3% sleeve / ±1.5% per line |
| **Alternatives** | Return sources not in listed markets; manager discretion inside wrapper | 9% | 12% | Cat II private credit (2), Cat III LS or SIF hybrid LS (1–2), pre-IPO/PE (Aggressive) | ±2%; no forced rebalancing |
| **Stabilisers** | Drawdown control and carry | 24% FI + 4% REIT/InvIT + 6% gold/silver | 8% + 2% + 5% | TMF index funds, 10-yr G-sec, AA credit funds, gold/silver ETF, 4–5 REIT/InvITs | ±3% FI / ±1.5% gold / ±1% REIT |
| **Liquidity** | Fee/tax/consent-latency buffer, deployment parking | 2% | 2% | Arbitrage fund, overnight fund | 1–4% hard range |

### 2.2 Instrument decision matrix

Score each candidate 1–5 on six criteria; weight cost 20%, tax 20%, liquidity 15%, capacity 15%, alpha evidence 15%, NDPMS consent friction 15%. Anything <3.0 is not used.

| Vehicle | Cost (bps p.a.) | Tax | Liquidity | Capacity at ₹500 Cr | Alpha evidence needed | NDPMS consent friction | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Index ETF via AP creation unit | 3–10 TER + 5–15 impact | Equity 12.5% LTCG >12m [12][13] | T+1/T+2 | Unlimited (Nifty BeES AUM ₹66,777 Cr; CU 50,000 units) [43][44] | None | Low | **Core beta, gold** |
| Index fund (direct) | 10–20 | Same | T+2/T+3 | Unlimited | None | Lowest — NAV order, no price risk in consent lag | **Core, factor, international** |
| Active MF (direct) | 60–110 | Equity 12.5%/20% | T+2/T+3 | Ticket ≤1% of scheme AUM | 3-yr rolling alpha >150 bps net in ≥60% of windows | Low | **Mid/small only** |
| Third-party PMS | 100–250 + perf | Pass-through; STCG churn risk | 1–4 weeks | Min ₹50 lakh [1][2] | 5-yr live, IR >0.4 | Low once onboarded | **One manager ≤3%** |
| Direct stocks | 0 TER; 15–40 impact | We control realisation | 1–3 days | ≤1% float, ≤20% ADV | Live scorecard record | **Highest** | **8–12% cap** |
| AIF Cat II | 150–200 + carry | Pass-through; interest at slab [14] | Locked 3–7 yrs [60][61] | ₹1 Cr min [7]; 25% unlisted cap [1][2] | DPI/IRR, default record | Low after commitment | **Private credit, PE** |
| AIF Cat III | 150–250 + perf | Fund-level up to ~42.7% [15] | Monthly/quarterly | ₹1 Cr min | Net-of-tax Sharpe >0.8 | Low | **Long-short** |
| SIF | 100–150 approx. | MF category taxation (verify per scheme) | Daily–quarterly, notice ≤15 working days [11] | ₹10 lakh min [9] | 12–18 months live | Low | **Prefer over Cat III LS once track exists** |
| Bonds direct | 0; 5–25 bid-offer | Coupon slab; LTCG 12.5% >12m listed | G-sec deep; corporate patchy | Corporate lots ₹1–5 Cr | None | Medium | **10-yr G-sec direct; corporate via funds** |
| REIT/InvIT | 0; 10–30 impact | Dividend part exempt; interest slab | 1–5 days | 4–5 names ≤₹6 Cr each | None | Low | **Stabiliser yield** |

**Active vs passive rule.** Passive unless the sleeve passes all three: (i) documented persistence of manager alpha in that segment (Indian mid/small yes; large cap no), (ii) our ticket ≤1% of scheme AUM, (iii) net-of-tax expected alpha exceeds the TER differential by ≥100 bps.

---

## 3. Model portfolios sized to ₹500 Cr

### 3.1 Moderate / balanced (target: house-benchmark return at ~70% of its risk)

## 5. Translating the monthly house view into TAA

### 5.1 Framework

1. **SAA is the contract.** Model Master weights + bands sit in the IPS schedule signed at onboarding. Band-restoring trades need only a confirmation.
2. **TAA is the IC's monthly vote**, expressed as conviction scores C ∈ {−3…+3} per view axis (large vs mid/small; quality vs value/momentum; duration; credit; gold; international; alternatives pace).
3. **Sizing:** tilt (pp) = C × unit, where unit = TE budget ÷ (Σ|C| × view vol), capped by the sleeve band. With TE budget 2.0% (Moderate) / 3.0% (Aggressive) vs own composite, a unit is ~1.0 pp Moderate / 1.5 pp Aggressive.
4. **Evidence bar:** a view must clear two of three — (a) valuation z-score |z| ≥1 vs 10-yr history, (b) earnings/macro revision breadth in the view's direction for ≥2 months, (c) scorecard pillar spread in top/bottom quintile. C=±3 requires all three plus IC unanimity.
5. **Decay:** each tilt carries a 6-month review; if not reaffirmed it halves automatically.

### 5.2 Worked example (Moderate, Sep-2026 IC): overweight large-cap quality (+2), underweight small cap (−2), duration long (+2), gold neutral (0)

| View axis | C | Unit (pp) | Tilt (pp) | From → To | ₹ Cr moved | Instrument | Band check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Large-cap quality | +2 | 1.0 | +2.0 | Quality factor 5 → 7 | +10 | Nifty 200 Quality 30 index fund | within ±2 |
| Small cap | −2 | 1.0 | −2.0 | Active small 3 → 1 | −10 | Redeem small-cap MF | breaches ±1 → cap at −1 (₹5 Cr), take remaining −1 from mid cap |
| Duration | +2 | 1.0 | +2.0 | 10-yr G-sec 6 → 8; TMF 11 → 9 | +10 / −10 | Direct G-sec 2036 | within ±2 |
| Gold | 0 | — | 0 | 5 → 5 | 0 | — | — |
| Net | | | | | ~₹35 Cr gross ≈ 7% turnover | | TE added ≈ 0.6% |

The consent pack that month has **5 TAA lines + band restorations**, all executable on the Thursday cycle.

## 6. Deployment plan for fresh ₹500 Cr

**Baseline: 12 weekly Thursday tranches for equity-like sleeves, 4 for fixed income, alternatives on manager drawdown schedules over 6–18 months.** Undeployed equity money sits in an arbitrage fund (6.2% E[R], equity-taxed) rather than a liquid fund (slab-taxed) — worth ~15 bps post-tax on the parked balance for a 39%-slab client.

| Week | Equity-like (60% Mod = ₹300 Cr) | Fixed income (24% = ₹120 Cr) | Alternatives (9% = ₹45 Cr) | Parked in arbitrage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | ₹25 Cr | ₹30 Cr | Commitments signed | ₹445 Cr |
| 1–3 | ₹25 Cr/wk | ₹30 Cr/wk (done wk 3) | — | ₹340 → ₹280 Cr |
| 4–11 | ₹25 Cr/wk | — | Drawdowns ~25%/qtr | ₹255 → ₹55 Cr |
| 12 | Final ₹25 Cr | — | — | ₹45 Cr |

**Acceleration rules (pre-consented in the schedule):** Nifty ≥5% below T → +1 tranche that week; ≥10% → +2; ≥15% → all remaining within 2 weeks; India VIX >22 for 3 days = −5% trigger; never decelerate on rallies (asymmetric rule avoids chasing); 10-yr yield +25 bps from T → pull forward the duration tranche.

**Expected cash drag:** equity-like sleeve over 12 weeks carries ~6.5 weeks of the ~5-point equity-minus-arbitrage gap → **≈ ₹2.0 Cr Moderate / ₹2.5 Cr Aggressive** (40–50 bps one-off). FI drag ≈ ₹0.05 Cr. Alternatives drag ≈ ₹1.2–1.6 Cr (committed, undrawn ~6 months). An 8-week schedule cuts equity drag to ₹1.4–1.7 Cr; at 20× P/E with the market already −6% off highs, the IC should choose 8 weeks with acceleration rules armed.

risks_and_pitfalls: Consent latency turns into a systematic cost: a 3-day lag on 20% NAV/year of trades has ~6 bps expected cost but ±30 bps 1σ; in a fast sell-off the acceleration tranches will execute days late unless they are pre-consented in the schedule.

Legal ambiguity on standing instructions: if a pre-authorised band-execution matrix is later judged to be discretion in disguise, the PM could be in breach; get a written opinion and design the pack to work without it.

Unlisted-cap creep: AIF NAVs lag and are smoothed, so in an equity drawdown of −30% a 12% unlisted sleeve becomes ~16% of NAV mechanically; set the internal alert at 18% and never commit above 15% at SAA.

International access risk: the USD 7 bn industry overseas cap has already forced AMCs to pause inflows (May 2026); a 5–7% sleeve may be unfillable for months, and redemptions elsewhere could reset our access.

Momentum and small-cap crash asymmetry: Smallcap 250 fell 69% in 2008 and took 591 trading days to recover post-COVID; Momentum 30 1-yr return is ~0% after a −60% approx. historical drawdown; sizing beyond the bands will dominate realised drawdown.

Tax drag is the largest owned cost (60–80 bps approx.): private-credit interest at ~39% slab and Cat III fund-level tax at ~42.7% can wipe out the alternatives' return advantage; run everything on post-tax expected return before sizing.

Correlation and volatility assumptions are approximate: primary index factsheets (niftyindices.com, NSE archives) were not reachable during this exercise, so vol/correlation inputs should be re-estimated from downloaded index histories before the IC signs the CMAs.

Benchmark mismatch politics: the Moderate book is designed to match the 80/20 house benchmark's return at 70% of its vol; if the client or RM judges only on headline return vs 80/20, the design will look like underperformance in bull years.

Liquidity mismatch in a redemption: 9–12% locked plus 4–5% in 30–90-day Cat III/SIF means a 25% client redemption would be met entirely from listed sleeves, distorting the SAA and forcing a consent cycle to rebalance.
Direct-stock book concentration and scorecard drift: 20–25 names at 8–12% NAV; a single 3% position halving costs 150 bps; every stock trade is a consent line so error-correction is slow.

Silver and gold regime risk: gold's 10-yr CAGR of 11–15% was front-loaded by central-bank buying; a reversal of the 2024–26 rally would hit 5–6% of NAV; silver's −54% historical drawdown justifies the 1% cap.

Manager and scheme-size risk in active MFs and PMS: a ₹25 Cr ticket into a scheme under ₹2,500 Cr AUM moves the manager's book; boutique small-cap capacity is limited and exit takes 3–10 days at best.

Private credit cycle risk: India private credit reached USD 3.5 bn in H1 2026 with softer returns and record defaults globally; senior-secured discipline and two-manager diversification are mandatory.

Regulatory change risk: SEBI's Jul-2026 PMS consultation (overseas investing, unlisted debt, MF-PMS) and Aug-2026 accredited-investor proposals could widen the toolkit or change the 25% unlisted definition; the SAA should have a regulatory-change review clause.
open_questions: Will the client sign a pre-authorised execution matrix for band-restoring trades within stated ranges, and does external counsel confirm this satisfies the non-discretionary 'client instruction' requirement under the PMS Regulations?
Which variant is the mandate — Moderate or Aggressive — and does the client accept the composite benchmark (Nifty 500 TRI-based) as primary with the Allocate 80/20 as secondary?
What is the client's marginal tax rate and entity type (individual/HUF/family trust/company)? Post-tax sizing of private credit, Cat III and debt funds depends entirely on this.

Is the client an SEBI accredited investor (or willing to obtain accreditation under the proposed ₹5 Cr securities-assets route)? This changes AIF minimums and potentially PMS large-value flexibilities.
What is the client's liquidity need profile: any planned withdrawals over 3 years, and is a 9–12% locked allocation acceptable?
How much drawdown can the client tolerate before instructing a de-risk — is the expected GFC-type −30% (Moderate) / −40% (Aggressive) explicitly acknowledged in the IPS?
Deployment speed: does the IC prefer 8 or 12 weeks given Nifty at ~20× trailing P/E and −6% off highs, and does the client accept the pre-consented acceleration rules?
Does the client already hold international, AIF or PMS positions elsewhere that we should net against (e.g., USD 7 bn cap access, existing AIF commitments)?
Which existing Allocate direct-stock names may be reused in the NDPMS direct book, and does the client accept holdings overlap with Allocate model portfolios?
Is the client willing to accept a SIF allocation despite the category's short (<18-month) live track record, in exchange for cheaper taxation than Cat III?
Should the performance fee (if any) be measured against the composite benchmark or the 80/20, and on pre- or post-tax returns?
Who at the client signs the monthly consent pack, in what turnaround time, and what is the fallback if the signatory is unavailable during a tail event?
